To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

solid solutions of calcium hydroxylapatite (CaHA) and leadhydroxylapatite(PbHA) of the chemical formula Ca10−Pb(PO4)6(OH)2 were prepared, and the lattice parameters and cation distributions were determined by XRD.
the lattice parameters of solid solutions of Ca10−x Pb x (PO4) 6 (OH) 2 varied linearly with the composition in the range 10−x 0<x<10.
the lattice parameters of the apatites varied linearly with the Pb/Ca ratio, and that all lead was found in the sixfold cation position.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of solid solutions of Ca10−x Pb x(PO4)6(OH)2 and their characterization.
the preparation, characterization and properties of lead containing hydroxyapatites, Pb10−x Ca x (PO4) 6(OH)2 (0<x<10) and their application in radiation therapy.
the synthesis of solid solution of calcium and lead apatites, the determination of lattice parameters and cation location.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PbOHA and CaOHA solid solution series have a limited miscibility gap in which the apatitic phases of PbOHA have a maximum in the range 2<x<4.

the solid solutions of CaOHA and lead apatite are apatitic in a limited range of Pb/Ca ratios and that the apatite solid solution series is not stable at the conditions used for the preparation of the samples.

the apatite solid solutions in the Ca10−x Pb x (PO4) 6 (OH) 2 system are miscible in the range 3.5<x<4.5 and immiscible in the range x>4.5, where the latter range is limited by the instability of PbOHA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

apatites of the type Pb10 P6 (PO4)2 (OH)6 are not stable in the range 800°C and 1 atm, whereas apatite solid solutions in the system CaOHA-PbOHA are stable in this range and have been prepared in this study.
the apatitic solid solutions of CaOHA and CdOHA are stable in the range 3<x<7, whereas Pb2+ is completely substituted for Ca2+ in the range 7<x<10.
the apatites of the formula Ca5+x Pb5−x (PO4)3 (OH) are stable in the range 2<x<6.
The main takeaway from our work is that

apatites with a Pb/Ca ratio in the range 3-5 can be obtained as pure phases by coprecipitating Ca and Pb phosphates and heating the precipitates at 800°C under CO2-free water vapour of 1 atm pressure.
the cation distribution in the solid solution of CaOHA-PbOHA is not random but rather the lead is exclusively in the sixfold site.
the Pb2+ cations in the apatitic structure can be substituted for Ca2+ without changing the symmetry of the structure.
